drafted.claim: Values of the risk aversion parameter ρ in the Solo and Social conditions were broadly consistent with the risk premium values.
drafted.why: The tree records the risk-premium null (risk-premiums-not-differ-between) and the ρ difference (participants-slightly-more-risk-averse) as separate results but nowhere that the two risk-attitude measures agree with each other, which is what licenses reading them as one construct rather than as a contradiction; the second result in this caption sentence, ρ being higher in Social than Solo in Study 1 only, is already carried by participants-slightly-more-risk-averse.

drafted.claim: A smaller left IFG cluster showed the same insula-seeded connectivity effect — highest when participants made Risky choices for themselves and Safe choices for both players — but did not survive correction for multiple tests (p uncorrected = 0.001, T = 4.08, Z = 3.97, 38 voxels, peak MNI [−38 –2 26]).
drafted.why: The tree's insula-seeded connectivity claim (functional-connectivity-between-left-anterior) records only the corrected right IFG cluster, and the one existing sub-threshold left IFG claim (left-ifg-cluster-showed-opposite) is a different cluster from the STS seed with the reversed pattern, so the bilateral, partly uncorrected extent of the insula-seeded effect is currently unrecorded.

drafted.claim: During the decision phase, the Risky–Safe BOLD response difference was greater in the Social than the Solo condition in the precuneus (0.30***) and left TPJ (0.24***), and smaller in the left ventral striatum (–0.47***) and mPFC (–0.10***).
drafted.why: The tree states in words that only precuneus and TPJ showed positive Risky–Safe differences in Social versus Solo (only-precuneus-tpj-showed-positive) but carries none of the coefficients, and in particular not the sign and size of the negative ventral striatum and mPFC effects that are what 'only' rests on; the run and socialVsSolo:run terms in the same table are a separate result and would need their own claim.

drafted.claim: During the decision phase, the Risky–Safe BOLD response difference was greater in the Social than the Partner condition in the precuneus (0.39***), mPFC (0.23***), and left TPJ (0.07**), and smaller in the left ventral striatum (–0.07***).
drafted.why: Every ROI claim in the tree for the decision phase compares Social with Solo; this is the Social-versus-Partner half of the pair, and it is the comparison in which mPFC is positive rather than negative, so without it the claim that only precuneus and TPJ are positive in both comparisons cannot be checked.
